assays.title: PTEN lipid phosphatase scores
assays.construct: Translated target matches canonical P60484 sequence version 1
assays.controls: Synonymous distribution: metadata describes wild-type-like interval [-1.11, 0.89].
assays.replicate_availability: Biological A/B and technical subreplicate aggregate scores are supplied; not treated as independent raw observations.
limitations: Scale and endpoint differ across assays; no shared normalization is performed.
Descriptive cross-assay patterns do not establish mechanism or disease effect.
assays.methods:
Pair-ended reads were merged with PEAR. Custom Python scripts were used to identify and count sequence variants. Variant count files were then analysed with Enrich2 v.1.2.0. Scores and standard errors were calculated for each variant. A variant was considered high-confidence if the 95% confidence interval of the fitness score was <= 1, or if measurements from each biological replicate were both lower or both higher than the 95% bound of the synonymous distribution.

Variants were considered wild-type like if they achieved a fitness score between the lower and upper 95th percentile (two-tailed) of synonymous variants, -1.11 and 0.89.

The score and SE columns are combined across all replicates as applicable. Scores and SE for each biological replicate (A and B) and technical replicate (A1, A2, etc.) are also provided.

assays.title: PTEN VAMP-seq Combined
assays.system: VAMP-seq abundance measurements; composite of original/fill-in datasets
assays.scale: published VAMP-seq abundance score; original scale (not clamped to 0–1)
assays.construct: Translated target matches canonical P60484 sequence version 1
assays.controls: Original method describes WT score 1 and average nonsense score 0; composite dataset averages available replicate scores.
assays.replicate_availability: Up to 15 per-replicate scores with missingness; exchangeability is not established.
assays.uncertainty_availability: Reported SE and confidence intervals retained.
limitations: Scale and endpoint differ across assays; no shared normalization is performed.
Descriptive cross-assay patterns do not establish mechanism or disease effect.
assays.methods: Abundance scores from the original and fill-in datasets were aggregated and a composite score was calculated by taking the mean of all 15 replicate scores (8 from the original, 7 for the fill-in).
assays.original_methods:
Barcodes for each bin were counted and associated with variant sequences using Enrich2. Scores were calculated based on the frequency of each variant in each bin using a weighted average such that increased abundance in high-signal bins gives a higher score. Abundance scores were calculated based on a min-max normalization using wild type (score of 1) and the average nonsense variant score (score of 0). The scores reported are the average of the eight replicate scores. Confidence intervals and variance estimates are based on the replicate scores.

Metadata contains the mapping between abundance classes and the integer values found in the database.

defaults.activity_cutoff_basis: Source methods lower synonymous interval boundary; exploratory selection, not a clinical threshold.
defaults.abundance_cutoff_basis: Derived 5th percentile of 193 reported synonymous-control scores using numpy linear quantile. Exploratory, not author-endorsed classification.

limitations: Activity is a humanized-yeast fitness proxy; abundance is a separate VAMP-seq endpoint.
Combining the two scores describes a pattern; it does not prove a causal mechanism.
Replicate scores are not automatically exchangeable raw biological replicates.
Protein-substitution measurements are not uniquely assigned DNA-allele measurements.
